preconditions.expression: all(0 <= A[i] < N or A[i] == -1 for i in range(N))
preconditions.description: Each element in A is either a non-negative integer less than N or -1 (lost element).
The length of A is exactly N.
The size of the permutation N is at least 1.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= P[i] <= N for i in range(N))
postconditions.description: The output permutation P contains integers from 1 to N exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(P[i] != P[j] for i in range(N) for j in range(N) if i != j)
postconditions.description: The output permutation P is a valid permutation (all elements are unique).

postconditions.expression: all((A[i] == 0 and all(P[i] > P[j] for j in range(i))) or (A[i] != 0 and A[i] == max(j for j in range(i) if P[j] > P[i]) if any(P[j] > P[i] for j in range(i)) else 0) for i in range(N))
postconditions.description: The output permutation P generates the input array A according to the given rules, where A[i] = -1 is treated as a wildcard (any valid value).

postconditions.expression: all(P[i] < P[j] for i in range(N) for j in range(N) if i < j and P[i] == P[j]) == False
postconditions.description: The permutation P is lexicographically smallest among all valid permutations.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or all(int(x) for x in stdout.strip().split()) == sorted(int(x) for x in stdout.strip().split())
postconditions.description: If no valid permutation exists, the output is '-1'; otherwise, the output is a valid permutation.
